comparator.name: Philosophy
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–2027 regulations (26 May 2026), English Philosophy track, supply a coherent annual curriculum of 180 EC: ten compulsory 6 EC first-year units, eight compulsory and two selected 6 EC second-year units, and 30 EC open study plus two selected 6 EC philosophy electives, Bachelor Seminar III (6 EC) and an individual philosophy thesis (12 EC). The restricted choices are Theoretical Philosophy: Capita Selecta and World Philosophies I in Year 2, then History of Philosophy: Capita Selecta and Issues in Contemporary Ethics in Year 3. Each is taken once. One World Philosophies I/II unit is required across Years 2–3; the selected I meets it. The 2026–2027 annual plan is the comparator snapshot, not a guarantee of future optional-course topics. The thesis requires the entire first year and 48 EC from Year 2; all are completed before the final-year thesis in this pathway. The individual thesis formulates a philosophical question, independently selects literature and develops an argument under supervision; two readers assess it. Bachelor Seminar III trains its proposal, argument, literature search, chapter writing and peer feedback. Zero-credit Philosophical Encounters I and II and the English language test remain separate obligations. The diagnostic test or completed refresher gates the Skills: Academic English grade; BSA requires 42 first-year EC and the language-test quality condition. Annual Political Philosophy includes a Broader Mind certificate that validates its grade, within its 6 EC. Prior examination-board consent is normally needed for open study; individual electives include at least 12 EC at level 300. Eligible University minors and listed minors are exempt from prior consent, but Philosophy and Practical Philosophy minors are excluded for Philosophy students and compulsory overlap must be replaced with permission. Tutorials normally require 80% attendance; course requirements also apply, including compulsory argumentation/text seminars, all Logic quizzes and 75% Logic lecture attendance, and at most one missed Text Course II meeting. Honours is additional. English-named Philosophy and ENG registry provenance select the English track before UCR fit; Dutch Filosofie PLUS religion/theology or governance variants are separate and not merged into it. The current Dutch recruitment page simplifies its basic-track structure; the adopted English track annual plan controls this comparator.

alternatives.label: Philosophy, argument and historical perspectives
alternatives.concept: Philosophical argument remains the central method: a Western philosophy introduction leads into ethics, mind, emotion, free will and political philosophy, with human-rights theory and logical reasoning. Rhetoric and literary interpretation develop related argument and reading skills; history, archaeology and global literature provide contexts. These complements do not supply specialist global histories of philosophy, epistemology, philosophy of science, or the sustained Plato/Kant text seminars and compulsory philosophy thesis at VU.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule contains direct philosophy courses and an argumentation strand, complemented by historical and intercultural sources.
progression: All48 placements verified directly from actual workbook offerings and prerequisites; all formal prerequisites are NONE. Introductory philosophy and political philosophy precede advanced philosophical work. In the first option rhetoric precedes Rhetoric in Action; the latter involves local primary-school children and principally Dutch interaction. In the second option climate science/justice/communication precede advanced sustainability project work; rhetorical persuasion has no formal introductory-rhetoric prerequisite. 24 unique courses180 EC,four per semester,Year 1PPD,at least6 advanced courses.

alternatives.label: Ethics, climate and public reasoning
alternatives.concept: Philosophical ethics, political philosophy, mind, emotion and agency organise questions of climate responsibility and public decisions. Climate science, environmental justice, economics, governance and media analysis provide specific problems and evidence for that inquiry. This is an applied ethical direction within a substantial philosophy programme; its sustainability project is group research and does not replace an individual philosophical thesis or specialist philosophical history.
alternatives.labelReason: Climate Change, Social Movements & Environmental Justice, Governance of Sustainability and related communication and economic courses ground the ethical questions in public decisions.
alternatives.distinctness: Seven courses/52.5 EC differ on each side. Climate Change, environmental justice, climate communication, economics, governance, regional sustainability research and environmental media replace seven rhetoric/literature/archaeology courses. Both retain substantive philosophical inquiry; one applies it to public environmental decisions, the other to argument and historical-cultural interpretation.

candidates.label: Practical philosophy of climate, markets and public decisions
candidates.assessment: Ethics and Political Philosophy include applied contemporary questions in the exact English track. Dutch PLUS governance rows are acknowledged as separate variant evidence, not used to assert an English formal governance route. UCR retains6 dedicated philosophy courses45 EC plus legal-philosophical and ethical-rhetorical work; seven climate/economic/governance courses provide a distinct application.

candidates.label: Theoretical philosophy of mind and knowledge
candidates.assessment: A separate theoretical option would reuse the five PHIL courses and logic already central to the closest option. Psychology/AI could add contexts but would change the disciplinary organising object; no distinct philosophical sequence is established.

candidates.label: Dutch-track PLUS philosophy with religion and theology
candidates.assessment: A genuine Dutch-track variant, outside the selected English comparator. No sustained UCR religion/theology sequence is established by myths, archaeological context or general philosophy. It is rejected, not implemented through adjacent subjects.

selection.assessment: Retain two qualified philosophical responses, with philosophy as the taught object and argument as its method, rather than replacing philosophy with generic cultural meaning. Six dedicated philosophy courses45 EC per option (five PHIL plus Political Philosophy), Human Rights law/philosophy and ethical persuasion establish substantive depth and progression; logical reasoning and contexts support it. This is not a matching quota or degree equivalence. Seven-course52.5 EC substitutions produce a real environmental/public-decisions direction. A third theoretical option repeats the same philosophical resources; Dutch PLUS religion/theology has neither selected-route status nor a sustained UCR disciplinary sequence. Stop at two.

notes.text: VU provides150 EC of philosophy plus30 EC open study, including global philosophical histories, specialist theoretical philosophy, Plato/Kant text seminars and a12 EC individual thesis. Both UCR options retain a progression in philosophical questions and argument, with historical-cultural or environmental/public-decision applications. Archaeology, mythology, empirical methods and governance provide complements; they do not fill those specialist gaps. Rhetoric in Action involves principally Dutch interaction with local schoolchildren. No philosophy degree equivalence, teaching qualification or automatic master’s admission is implied.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Philosophy studies fundamental questions through historical, practical and theoretical philosophy. Students learn philosophical argument, analyse demanding texts and develop an independent thesis. The English track combines150 EC of philosophy with30 EC of elective or minor space.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Two qualified UCR alternatives keep philosophical questions and argument central. One develops historical-cultural interpretation and rhetoric; the other applies ethics and political philosophy to climate responsibility and public decisions. Their complementary courses do not reproduce VU’s global philosophical histories, specialist text seminars or required individual thesis.

curriculum.limitation: The180 EC path selects World PhilosophiesI and Theoretical Philosophy in Year 2, then History of Philosophy and Contemporary Ethics in Year 3. Thesis entry requires allYear 1 subjects and48 EC fromYear 2. Language testing or a refresher gates Academic English; zero-credit seminars remain required. Political Philosophy includes Broader Mind participation. Open electives have approval, level and overlap rules; course attendance conditions apply. Optional topics and future offerings can change.
